claims.name: abs_M_two_A_iff

claims.doc: P025_body.tex:190 (claim N1): "Part (a) is a classical inequality (on `|z|=1` it says `|H'(z)| ≤ |(H^*)'(z)|` ...)", for `H` of degree at most `n` with no zero in `𝔻` (the hypotheses of Lemma 2.2) and `|z| = 1`.

claims.name: lem_2_2_a_zero
claims.doc: P025_body.tex:230: "At a zero of `H` on the circle the inequality in (a) is an equality" (proved at every zero).

claims.name: eq_one_factor

claims.name: lem_2_2_b
claims.doc: Lemma 2.2(b), P025_body.tex:203-208: `K(z,η) = (H(z) conj H(η) - H*(z) conj H*(η)) / (1 - z η̄) = Σ K_ij z^i η̄^j` — multiplied out for all `z, η`, and as a quotient where `z η̄ ≠ 1` — and `(K_ij)` is positive semidefinite.

claims.name: schurCohn_unique
claims.doc: Support for Lemma 2.2(b) ("its coefficient matrix", P025_body.tex:208): the identity of `lem_2_2_b` determines the matrix, so `schurCohn` IS the coefficient matrix of `K(z,η)` (no hypothesis on the zeros).

claims.name: lem_2_2_c
claims.doc: Lemma 2.2(c), eq. (eq:entries), P025_body.tex:209-213 (no hypothesis on the zeros needed).

claims.name: exists_max_circle
claims.doc: Support (P025_body.tex:42, 259: "let `|ζ| = 1` with `|P(ζ)| = M(P)`"): `M(P)` is attained on the circle.

claims.name: thm_3_1
claims.doc: Theorem 3.1, P025_body.tex:258-262 (open discs); also P025_body.tex:125 ("That no open disc of radius larger than `M/2` lies in `P(𝔻)` is elementary": this row uses no cited result).

claims.name: lem_3_2
claims.doc: Lemma 3.2, P025_body.tex:269-272 ("it also covers polynomials of degree less than `n`", P025_body.tex:267).

claims.name: lem_3_2_closed
claims.doc: Support for Lemma 3.2 (P025_body.tex:264-265: de Bruijn's theorem, "quoted in [OR74, p. 332] for open and closed circular regions"): the CLOSED disc of Lemma 3.2 lies in the image of the closed unit disc.

claims.name: prop_3_3
claims.doc: Proposition 3.3, P025_body.tex:280-283, with "In particular `F'(ζ) ≠ 0`" (P025_body.tex:292-293); also the Table's and the introduction's "point of maximum modulus, where `ζP'(ζ) = (n/2) P(ζ)`" (P025_body.tex:75-76, 122), and the sketch's "the first fact, applied at a point `ζ` where `|P|` is largest, places every omitted value at distance at least `M/2` from `P(ζ)/2`" (P025_body.tex:138-139: the disc below, for every omitted value).

claims.name: thm_3_4
claims.doc: Theorem 3.4 [Kr79, Kr80, OR74, SS74], P025_body.tex:308-311 — the ONE cited result: the Cited/ input `coef_half_max`, restated with `maxMod` and `ZerosOnCircle` (status CITED).

claims.name: coef_note_trig
claims.doc: The note after Theorem 3.4, P025_body.tex:313-319 (claim N2; `n = 2m`, `m = n/2`). For `P` of degree `2m ≥ 2` with all zeros on the unit circle: by Lemma 2.1 `P* = λP` with `|λ| = 1`; for EVERY such `λ`, `Q(θ) = e^{-imθ} P(e^{iθ})` (`= trigT 1 m P θ`) satisfies `conj Q = λ Q` (real `θ`); a `c` with `c^2 = λ` exists, and for EVERY such `c`, `T = cQ` (`= trigT c m P`) has `|c| = 1`, is real on the real line, is the trigonometric polynomial `Σ_{j=0}^{2m} c a_j e^{i(j-m)θ}` (all complex `θ`) of exact degree `m` (top coefficient `c a_n ≠ 0`); its zeros: `P` has `2m` zeros counted with multiplicity, `T(θ) = 0` iff `P(e^{iθ}) = 0` (complex `θ`), every zero `θ` of `T` is real, and `t ↦ e^{it}` maps the zeros of `T` in the period `[0, 2π)` one-to-one onto the zeros of `P` ("its `2m` zeros in a period are all real"); `max |T| = sup |T| = M(P)`; its constant term `t_0 = (1/2π) ∫_0^{2π} T` is `c a_{n/2}`; and "the case `k = n/2` says that the constant term `t_0` of such a `T` satisfies `|t_0| ≤ (1/2) max |T|`" (P025_body.tex:318-319): `|a_m| ≤ M(P)/2` iff `|c a_m| ≤ (1/2) sup |T|`.

claims.name: cor_3_5
claims.doc: Corollary 3.5, P025_body.tex:321-323 (Theorem 3.1 with Theorem 3.4: this row passes the cited result).

claims.name: thm_4_1
claims.doc: Theorem 4.1 (the covering theorem), P025_body.tex:334-340; abstract P025_body.tex:15-16; Table P025_body.tex:69-70; P025_body.tex:84-87. Its only input beyond Lean's three standard ones is the cited Theorem 3.4 (the abstract's Lean sentence, P025_body.tex:30-31: "with the coefficient bound ... taken as given").

claims.name: thm_4_1_case1
claims.doc: Theorem 4.1, Case 1 (`a_0 = 0`), P025_body.tex:346-353; idea of the proof P025_body.tex:139-140.

claims.name: thm_4_1_normalize
claims.doc: Theorem 4.1, Case 2, the normalization, P025_body.tex:355-357 (idea P025_body.tex:140: "we normalize so that `a_0 = a_n = 1`"): `a_n ≠ 0`, `P` has degree `n`; for `|α| = 1` with `α^n = a_0/a_n`, `Q(z) = P(αz)/a_0` has `q_0 = q_n = 1`, degree at most `n`, (eq:mirror), `Q(𝔻) = P(𝔻)/a_0`, and `A(Q) = A/|a_0| ≥ 1`.

claims.name: thm_4_1_case2_diag
claims.doc: Theorem 4.1, Case 2 (`a_0 = a_n = 1`), P025_body.tex:359-365; idea P025_body.tex:140-141: every diagonal entry of the Schur-Cohn matrix of `H = P - w` equals `d = |1 - w|^2 - 1`; for an omitted `w`, `|w - 1| ≥ 1`; if `A = 1`, `D(1,1) ⊆ P(𝔻)`.

claims.name: sketch_disc_one
claims.doc: The idea of the proof, P025_body.tex:140-141 (coverage link): with `a_0 = a_n = 1`, "the diagonal entries `K_jj` all equal `|1-w|^2-1 ≥ 0`, so `|1-w| ≥ 1`, which gives `D(1,1) ⊂ P(𝔻)`" — every omitted `w` has `|1-w|^2 - 1 ≥ 0` and `|1-w| ≥ 1`, and `D(1,1) ⊆ P(𝔻)` for EVERY `A`.

claims.name: eq_minor
claims.doc: Eq. (eq:minor), P025_body.tex:367-372; idea P025_body.tex:142-144: if `A > 1` (with `a_0 = a_n = 1`), `A` is attained at some `1 ≤ j ≤ n-1`; for every such `j`, `E = a_{n-j}/conj(a_j)` has `|E| = 1` (and does not depend on `w`), and every omitted `w` (`u = w - 1`) has `A |u + E| ≤ |u|^2 - 1`.

claims.name: eq_punctured
claims.doc: Eq. (eq:punctured), P025_body.tex:373-378; idea P025_body.tex:143-144 ("`|w-(1+E)| ≥ A` unless `w = 1-E`. Consequently every value in `D(1+E,A)` is taken, except possibly the single value `w_* = 1-E`"): `D(1+E, A) \ {w_*} ⊆ P(𝔻)`.

claims.name: thm_4_1_wstar
claims.doc: Theorem 4.1, Case 2, P025_body.tex:380-384; idea P025_body.tex:144-146: if `w_* = 1 - E` is omitted, then `S = P - w_*` has degree `n`, constant term `E`, leading coefficient 1, all zeros on the unit circle, `A(S) = A`, and `P(𝔻) = S(𝔻) + w_*`.

claims.name: rem_4_2_dist
claims.doc: Remark 4.2, P025_body.tex:388-389: `|w_* - (1+E)| = 2`, so `w_*` lies in `D(1+E, A)` only when `A > 2`.

claims.name: rem_4_2_no_coef
claims.doc: Remark 4.2, P025_body.tex:388-390: Theorem 3.4 "is needed only when `A > 2|a_0|` and `w_*` is omitted" — (i) without any cited input, Theorem 4.1 holds when `a_0 = 0` or `A ≤ 2|a_0|`.

claims.name: rem_4_2_wstar_taken
claims.doc: Remark 4.2, P025_body.tex:380, 389-390 — (ii) without any cited input, when `w_*` is taken (normalized `P`): "otherwise (eq:punctured) already gives `D(1+E,A) ⊂ P(𝔻)`".

claims.name: rem_4_2_off_middle
claims.doc: Remark 4.2, P025_body.tex:391-392: "if `A` is attained at some index `j ≠ n/2`, then `A(S) = |a_j|` with `j ≠ n/2`, and [OR74, Theorem 3] or [SS74, Theorem 3] suffices": Theorem 4.1 follows from the coefficient bound for `k ≠ n/2` alone (hypothesis `hOR`, the statement of [OR74, Thm 3] and [SS74, Thm 3] for `k ≠ n/2`).

claims.name: rem_4_2_middle_only
claims.doc: Support for Remark 4.2, P025_body.tex:392-393: the middle case is not needed unless `n` is even and `|a_{n/2}|` is strictly larger than every other `|a_k|` (the first two of the four conditions of `rem_4_2_middle_used_only`).

claims.name: rem_4_2_middle_used_only
claims.doc: Remark 4.2, P025_body.tex:392-393 (coverage link): "the middle case of Theorem 3.4, due to Kristiansen, is used only when `n` is even, `|a_{n/2}|` is strictly larger than every other `|a_k|` and than `2|a_0|`, and `w_*` is omitted": unless all four hold, Theorem 4.1 follows from the bound for `k ≠ n/2` alone (hypothesis `hOR`). `w_*` is `1 - E` for the normalized `Q = P(αz)/a_0` and `j = n/2`; "`w_*` is omitted" is stated for every admissible `α` (with `a_0 ≠ 0`: Case 1 has no `w_*`).

claims.name: rem_4_2_equiv
claims.doc: Remark 4.2, P025_body.tex:393-395: "The middle case cannot be bypassed: by Theorem 3.1, for polynomials with all zeros on the unit circle Theorem 4.1 is equivalent to Theorem 3.4": the covering statement is equivalent to the coefficient bound, and, given the cases `k ≠ n/2`, to the middle case.

claims.name: ex_5_1
claims.doc: Example 5.1, P025_body.tex:433-436 and P025_body.tex:110-111.

claims.name: ex_5_2
claims.doc: Example 5.2, P025_body.tex:440-451 ("here `E = 1`, and `w_* = 0` is taken because `P(z) = 0` when `z^m` is the root of `t^2+at+1` in `(-1,0)` ..., so the disc of the proof is `D(2,a)`", P025_body.tex:448-450).

claims.name: fig2_cardioid
claims.doc: Figure 2, left (caption P025_body.tex:426-428; label P025_body.tex:412): `(1+z)^2` maps the circle onto the cardioid `ρ = 2 + 2 cos ψ`; `P(𝔻)` is the region it bounds (`0 < ρ < 2 + 2 cos ψ`, `w = ρ e^{iψ}`); all zeros on the circle; `M = 4`, `A = 2`; the largest disc inside is `D(2,2)` (radius `M/2 = A`, and no other disc of radius 2 lies inside).

claims.name: fig2_limacon
claims.doc: Figure 2, right (caption P025_body.tex:428-430; label P025_body.tex:424; picture P025_body.tex:415-425): `1 + 4z + z^2` maps the circle onto the limaçon `ρ = 4 + 2 cos ψ`; `P(𝔻)` is the region it bounds (`ρ < 4 + 2 cos ψ`); it lies in the strip `-2 < Re w < 6`; the disc `D(2,4)` lies in it and has the largest possible radius `A = 4`; and "the grey disc is `D(3,3)`, of radius `M/2`" (P025_body.tex:430): `M = 6` and `D(3,3) ⊆ P(𝔻)`.

claims.name: abs_self_inversive
claims.doc: Abstract P025_body.tex:13-15, Table P025_body.tex:69-70, P025_body.tex:86-87: Sheil-Small's question has the answer yes: every self-inversive `P` maps `𝔻` onto a domain containing an open disc of radius `A`.

claims.name: abs_zeros_conj_inv
claims.doc: Abstract P025_body.tex:16-17 ("the self-inversive polynomials, whose zeros are symmetric with respect to the unit circle"), P025_body.tex:46-47 and 109-110 (Sheil-Small's own reading, zeros symmetric under `ζ ↦ 1/ζ̄`): such a `P` (degree `≥ 1`, `P(0) ≠ 0`) has an open disc of radius `A` in `P(𝔻)`.

claims.name: abs_zeros_inv
claims.doc: Abstract P025_body.tex:17-19 ("the polynomials whose zeros, with multiplicity, are symmetric under taking reciprocals (the literal reading of the problem as printed)"), P025_body.tex:106-110, the problem as printed P025_body.tex:55-57 (zeros symmetric under `ζ ↦ 1/ζ`).

claims.name: abs_plus_minus
claims.doc: P025_body.tex:107 (the literal reading in coefficient form, `a_{n-k} = ±a_k`, non-constant; Figure 1's dashed oval, P025_body.tex:97-98).

claims.name: intro_covering_implies_coef
claims.doc: P025_body.tex:127-129: "By Theorem 3.1, a positive answer for self-inversive polynomials also implies the theorem of O'Hara-Rodriguez, Saff-Sheil-Small and Kristiansen, so any proof of this answer also proves that theorem": the covering statement for the polynomials with all zeros on the circle (a subclass of the self-inversive ones, so this row assumes less) implies Theorem 3.4.
